title: Orion AI disaster recovery, SSO/KMS & SLA tabletop

Action items: share redacted SOC2, draft runbook for a cold failover test, propose warm-standby topology + cost estimate.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58 minutes | Attendees: Ethan Cole (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood Solutions), Mark Hsu (Orion SRE), Leah Kim (Orion Security Manager), Vikram Shah (Orion Cloud Eng), Anna Torres (Orion Compliance)

00:00 Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time, um we'll run through our incident response and BCDR tabletop focusing on SSO/KMS and SLA mechanics.
00:12 Mark: Thanks Ethan, quick context — Orion's latency-sensitive inference pipelines serve customer-facing features, we're evaluating Private deployment behind our VPC to meet residency and compliance.
00:24 Samira: Great, and to confirm, you said key concerns are RTO/RPO, audit trail access, and having customer-managed keys?
00:30 Mark: Yep, and also how Redwood handles escalation when there is a region outage and what warm standby looks like.
00:38 Leah: Plus we need to confirm RBAC mapping from our Okta groups to Redwood roles, and SAML flows, SCIM provisioning.
00:45 Diego: At a high level we support SAML 2.0, SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC can be mapped to tenant+role constructs; there are manuals, but we can show an export mapping.
00:58 Vikram: Our infra team will insist on KMS in our account with HSM-backed keys if possible, is customer-managed KMS supported?
01:05 Samira: Yes — for Private we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-kms). You can provide AWS KMS ARN or an HSM-backed key; Redwood can be configured to use that for model artifact encryption and live request payload encryption at rest. Note that envelope encryption patterns are used so Redwood never stores plaintext.
01:22 Anna: When you say "we" use a KMS, do you mean Redwood rotates, or does customer retain rotation control?
01:29 Samira: You retain key control. Rotation can be handled by your KMS lifecycle; Redwood will accept the new key versions as long as access policies allow. We do recommend a versioned key alias for smooth rotation.
01:40 Mark: What about audit logs and retention? Our compliance team requires 7 years for certain records and legal hold support.
01:48 Ethan: We expose audit logs via the Console and S3 export. Retention defaults depend on plan; for Private we can set long retention windows and deliver to your S3 bucket or our s3-compatible export with encryption. For legal holds, we can mark objects non-deletable if required.
02:05 Leah: Are those logs tamper-evident? We need integrity guarantees for SOC 2 audits.
02:11 Diego: We use append-only logging to a write-once bucket and can generate SHA256 digests for batches; we can also integrate with your SIEM via streaming. Admittedly transcript here: "writetime" sometimes transcribed as "write time" — sorry, try to ignore.
02:30 Mark: On RTO/RPO, what's typical for warm-standby vs cold? We're aiming for RTO under 15 minutes for critical inference routes and RPO under 5 minutes.
02:42 Samira: Warm-standby (replicated model cache + regional priming) can typically achieve 2-10 minute RTO depending on model size and KV priming. RPO depends on cache replication cadence; with near-real-time replication you can hit sub-5 minute RPOs but it's costlier. Cold failover (rebuild from artifacts) is hours.
03:00 Ethan: A couple of notes — for very large LLMs the KV cache and tokenizer priming add time; we do prefix caching but initial tokenization and KV warming is the main driver.
03:12 Mark: So warm-standby isn't free, what's the rough cost delta?
03:16 Samira: We'll send a model-size-specific estimate, but rule-of-thumb is 1.5-2.5x baseline for reserved warm capacity depending on model quant and memory. We'll put numbers in the follow-up.
03:30 Leah: Escalation — who do we call for P1s? We need a 24/7 paging path and phone fallback.
03:38 Diego: We recommend PD integration; Redwood has a primary on-call plus an escalation to engineer leads. Phone escalation is available for enterprise plans. Typical matrix: triage engineer -> SE lead -> oncall manager -> CTO escalation if necessary.
03:54 Mark: Can we see a sample runbook step for a region-isolated outage? Let's walk through it.
04:02 Samira: Sure — Step 1: Detect via health checks and error rates. Step 2: Auto-fail requests by policy to warm-standby region. Step 3: Notify via PagerDuty, post to incident channel, capture request IDs for replay. Step 4: For partial capacity loss, switch routing rules to degrade to smaller model variant (fallback) while investigating. Step 5: RTO target depends on whether KV cache was replicated.
04:35 Anna: For legal/forensics, what evidence will you provide post-incident?
04:40 Ethan: We'll provide timestamps, request IDs, audit logs, CPU/GPU utilization snapshots, and a postmortem with timeline. For Private we can deliver more granular host-level logs subject to support agreement.
04:52 Mark: How fast can we get operator access if we need to run an emergency KMS key revoke?
04:58 Samira: You control the key; Redwood won't be able to decrypt without permission. For emergency, we have a documented process to coordinate key rotation with a joint runbook — we do not hold master keys for customer-managed KMS.
05:12 Vikram: What about SLA credits — how are they calculated for multi-region?
05:18 Diego: Uptime measured at the route/model level; credits are prorated by downtime per SLO window, and multi-region setups can reduce single-region impact. SLA details are in the contract; for Dedicated/Private enterprise we support 99.95+ targets with specific credits.
05:33 Mark: Does Redwood perform cross-region failover testing with customers?
05:38 Ethan: Yes, we encourage tabletop and actual failover tests. Those are scoping sessions — we can run a controlled failover with a pre-defined test plan and can support a rehearsal including traffic shifts.
05:50 Leah: For SOC 2 evidence, can we get a snapshot of controls relevant to BCDR?
05:56 Ethan: We'll include control mappings in the artifact bundle. We'll also share the SOC 2 Type II report and the ISO scope.
06:05 Anna: On retention, are there e-discovery export capabilities for legal hold?
06:09 Diego: Yes — we can export filtered logs and requests to your bucket with an on-demand hold flag.
06:16 Mark: A few quick edge questions — what about KV cache poisoning or cache replay during failover?
06:22 Samira: We sign KV entries and validate freshness; during failover we replay only verified commits and can roll back to last consistent snapshot to avoid corrupt state.
06:33 Speaker 1: (crosstalk) and uh, sorry, who owns retries in the application layer?
06:38 Ethan: App typically owns idempotency and retries; Redwood supports idempotent request IDs and dedup semantics to help.
06:46 Vikram: If we choose Private with customer KMS, what network requirements do you need?
06:51 Samira: We'll need peering or transit gateway connectivity, egress rules for metrics and heartbeats, and ports for control plane sync. We'll share a network worksheet.
07:03 Mark: Can we get a sample runbook for a warm-standby failover?
07:07 Samira: We'll draft one in the follow-up; it'll include step-by-step commands, PD escalation ids, and smoke test URLs.
07:16 Anna: Any red flags from your side about our proposed constraints?
07:19 Diego: The main tradeoffs are cost vs RTO; also model size affects wake-up time. If RTO < 5 minutes is non-negotiable, expect significant standing capacity.
07:34 Leah: For compliance, are we asking you to sign anything specific for evidence access?
07:39 Ethan: We typically include support addendum for evidence access and audit cooperation; can add language about exports, signed NDAs if needed.
07:48 Mark: What's the cadence for joint DR drills?
07:51 Samira: Quarterly tabletop; annual live failover or as mutually agreed.
07:58 Diego: We'll also provide a checklist for a smoke test after failover — token tests, model sanity checks, latency sampling.
08:10 Speaker 2: (laugh) nice, okay next steps — um we should lock dates.
08:15 Ethan: Quick recap of next steps and owners — (Ethan) send SOC2/ISO, (Samira) draft warm standby topology, (Mark) share SAML metadata, (Vikram) network CIDRs, (Anna) confirm retention. We'll follow up with calendar invites.
08:35 Mark: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
08:38 Leah: Thank you.
08:40 End meeting.

Note: timestamps above are the first ~9 minutes condensed; the remainder of the call covered detailed Q&A and live screen-sharing of a sample runbook; some speaker attributions mid-call may be imperfect due to transcription.
